help.paymentDate: For cash-basis accounting, the actual payment date is generally decisive.
help.vatRate: General Austrian VAT rates: 20% standard rate and reduced rates of 10% and 13%. Use 0% only for exempt supplies or a specific zero rate.
help.inputVatDeductible: Input VAT is VAT on incoming invoices. It is generally deductible only for business use, with a compliant invoice and an existing right to deduct input VAT.
help.deductiblePercent: This share is documented as business-related. Deviations should be justified.
help.hospitalityDeductibility: Business meals are generally 50% deductible for income-tax purposes when an advertising purpose and predominantly business reason are documented; input VAT may remain fully deductible when the requirements are met.
help.taxDeductibility: Income tax and corporation tax on the entity's own profit are generally not deductible business expenses. Payroll-related and other business levies may be deductible; review the individual case.
help.nonVatAmount: Grants, SVS payments, taxes and levies are recorded here without a VAT split.
help.businessPurpose: The specific business reason helps substantiate hospitality expenditure.
help.participants: Names or a traceable group of the business contacts entertained.
help.advertisingPurpose: For business meals, evidence of an advertising purpose can affect tax treatment.
help.kilometreAllowance: The suggestion uses €0.50 per kilometre. The applicable rule must be reviewed before production use.
help.vehicleType: Different input VAT rules apply to cars, fiscal commercial vehicles and zero-emission vehicles.
help.inputVatVehicle: Input VAT is often excluded for passenger cars and estates. Exceptions require evidence.
help.usefulLife: Tax depreciation period. In 2026, depreciable assets costing up to €1,000 can generally be expensed immediately as low-value assets (net where input VAT is deductible, otherwise gross); above that, use the applicable useful life.
help.svsAuthority: SVS contributions for 2026 depend on the contribution basis; general rates are 18.5% pension insurance, 6.8% health insurance and 1.53% self-employed provision, plus accident insurance.
help.taxAuthority: Typical recipients are the Austrian Tax Office, a municipality or city, and the Austrian Economic Chamber. Follow the assessment notice or tax return.
help.levyType: Common Austrian taxes and levies in 2026: VAT 20/13/10%, corporation tax 23%, income tax progressively 0–55%, DB 3.7%, DZ 0.31–0.40% by state, and municipal tax 3%.
help.assessmentPeriod: Enter the period shown on the assessment notice or return, for example 2026, Q2/2026 or 07/2026.
